![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/d4573a2e3c7b220ac363c996c5332a3db93cc48b5b941e46a529b6912804f0c6.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-{y}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2-y-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z.$
question.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-{y}^{2},\,\,0\le x\le 2-y-z\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{0}^{2-y-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/8d1db6e886f00596814900ca0c4113590a37a407b65c800eb1f9926328ade50c.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 1-{y}^{2}\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ is 

$$
z=1-{y}^{2}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{1-z}.
$$

and the left boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-z}\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/1fe8a810a7e98c8a40739d5019ff9054a5375c0a12ae7fd1b17f8b6c8bb19f75.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-z}}{\int }_{0}^{2-y-z}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$
